quizzes.stem: A team wants an agent that studies a legacy system and cannot change a file. What goes in its definition?

options.a: The shell tool, with a rule that blocks redirections
options.b: A prompt sentence that tells it never to modify a file
options.c: No tools line, as leaving it out gives the smallest set
options.d: A tools line that lists only reading and searching tools

explanation.d: The tools line is the limit.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a prompt does not limit tools: "A sentence in the prompt is a request that the model weighs".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the omission is the widest list: "leaving the line out grants the most, not the least".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the shell is a way to write: "The shell tool can write files through redirections and commands".

quizzes.stem: A boilerplate agent may change files only in `src/generated`. Which settings give that?

options.a: An allow rule for the Edit tool, limited to that folder
options.b: An allow rule for the Write tool, limited to that folder
options.c: An allow rule for the whole Edit tool, plus a prompt naming the folder
options.d: A deny rule for the shell tool, since only commands can write

explanation.a: An Edit rule covers every built-in file-editing tool and a path keeps it to one folder.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a Write path rule is never read: "A path rule written for the Write tool is accepted and never consulted".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a bare rule has no path: "A bare `Edit` rule has no path and approves every edit."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the file tools have rules of their own: "Denying the shell does not limit the file tools".

quizzes.stem: A ticket server lets a caller fetch, add and remove tickets, and agents may only look at them. Which settings give that?

options.a: Deny the delete tool in the settings with a rule that matches on the ticket number
options.b: Allow every tool of the server, and tell the agents to read only
options.c: Allow the get tool by name, and deny the create and delete tools by name
options.d: Deny the whole server, then allow its get tool by name

explanation.c: Allow by name and deny the others by name.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a sentence is no limit: "A sentence in the prompt is a request that the model weighs".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rule is skipped: "In a settings file, a rule for an MCP tool that carries parentheses is skipped, so it matches nothing".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a deny rule beats every allow: "A matching deny rule wins over any allow rule, whatever the specificity."

quizzes.stem: A developer adds a header that reads a new environment name in the shared connection settings and leaves the team write-up alone. What does the practice's grading do?

options.a: The credentials case fails, since each new variable needs a default value
options.b: The documentation case fails, because one of the variables the servers use is unlisted
options.c: Nothing fails, since the write-up is advice that the grading never reads
options.d: The server case fails, since a header may not refer to any variable

explanation.b: The note has to list every variable: "every variable that appears in `.mcp.json` has to appear in the note."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the token has no default: "The token has none, because a default for a token would be a credential in the file".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the note is checked: "The check turns a convention into a rule that fails when someone adds a variable and forgets the note."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a shared file does refer to variables: "A committed `.mcp.json` refers to variables and cannot hold their values."

quizzes.stem: Which allow rules pass the practice's scaffolder case?

explanation.d: One Edit rule limited to the generated folder: "every allow rule that edits or writes is an `Edit` rule limited to `src/generated/`".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a Write path rule is never read: "a `Write(...)` path rule fails it, because Claude Code never consults it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the path is wider than the folder: "an `Edit` rule limited to `src/generated/`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because it adds a Write path rule: "a `Write(...)` path rule fails it, because Claude Code never consults it".

quizzes.stem: A new colleague clones the repository, and the ticket tools answer with an authorization error. The shared configuration is committed. What should the repository hold to prevent this?

options.a: A default for the token, written into the shared project file
options.b: A team note that names every variable that the servers need to start
options.c: A private copy of the project file with a working token in it, kept outside version control
options.d: A line in the root memory file that holds a shared token

explanation.b: A note makes the missing variables visible.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a default for a token is a credential in the file: "a default for a token would be a credential in the file".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a second copy defeats the shared file: "The file exists to be shared".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a committed file cannot hold a value: "A committed `.mcp.json` refers to variables and cannot hold their values."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. A check reports `unknown-server: wiki (explorer)`. What does the finding mean?

options.a: A header holds a credential that somebody typed in by hand, in plain text
options.b: A reference points at an entry that the project file never defines
options.c: A subagent has no tools line and inherits everything
options.d: A permission rule approves the whole tool rather than one path of it

explanation.b: The finding is about a name that is not configured.
explanation.a: Ruled out because that is another finding: "`literal-secret`: a header or environment entry whose name says token, key, secret or authorization".
explanation.c: is ruled out for the same reason: "`agent-inherits-all` and `agent-bare-bash`: a subagent with no `tools` line, or with the shell tool in it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because that is a third: "`bare-write-allowed`: an allow rule that approves the whole `Edit` or `Write` tool."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. Which entry does the check for typed-in credentials report?

options.a: A header named Authorization whose value is `Bearer example-token-123`
options.b: A header named Authorization whose value is `Bearer ${TICKETS_TOKEN}`
options.c: A header named X-Trace whose value is `abc`, sent with every request
options.d: A variable named REGION whose value is `eu`, passed to the local server

explanation.a: The check reports a secret-looking name whose value has no reference: "a header or environment entry whose name says token, key, secret or authorization and whose value has no `${` reference".
explanation.b: Ruled out because its value is a reference: "whose value has no `${` reference".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the name says nothing of a secret: "whose name says token, key, secret or authorization".
explanation.d: is ruled out for the same reason: "whose name says token, key, secret or authorization".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. Exploring a big module would fill the main conversation with file contents. What keeps the main context small?

options.a: A read-only subagent does the reading and hands back its result
options.b: A longer root memory file that summarises the module in advance
options.c: A forked session that begins with the history of the main one
options.d: A rule that denies the shell tool during every exploration

explanation.a: A subagent keeps what it reads in its own context.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a memory file does not move the reading: "the root file loads in every session and costs context each time".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a fork copies the history: "copies the history into a new session".
explanation.d: Ruled out because denying a tool does not move any reading elsewhere: "Denying the shell does not limit the file tools".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a helper that explores a legacy system and generates boilerplate. A team writes the header as `Bearer ${TICKETS_TOKEN:-dev-token}` so the tools work on a fresh clone. What is wrong with it?

options.a: A default is applied to the address and never to a header
options.b: Expansion in headers handles only the plain form of a reference
options.c: The default puts a usable credential into a committed file
options.d: A file that carries a default cannot be shared through version control

explanation.c: A default for a token is a credential in the file.
explanation.b: Ruled out because expansion has both forms: "Expansion of `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` works in a server's `command`, `args`, `env`, `url` and `headers`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a header is one of the places where it works: "`${VAR:-default}` expands to the variable if it is set and to the default otherwise".
explanation.d: Ruled out because sharing is the file's purpose: "The `.mcp.json` of a project is committed so that the team shares its servers."
